declarations.docstring: The linear equivalence between morphisms of finite biproducts and families of component morphisms.
The dimension of the morphism space from one value of a family to another.
Distinct elements of a finite indexing type yield two square matrices that do not commute.
The dimension of morphisms between finite biproducts is the double sum of the component dimensions.
Computes the dimension of the opposite endomorphism object associated with a family and multiplicities.
Characterizes when the displayed endomorphism dimension is the unweighted sum of morphism-space dimensions.
For constant multiplicity one, the opposite endomorphism dimension is the sum of all morphism-space dimensions.
Computes the dimension of the endomorphism object as a sum over pairs of indexed summands.
Square matrices over a subsingleton finite index type commute under multiplication.
A nontrivial endomorphism space has dimension at least one.
With positive dimensions, all displayed square matrix products commute exactly when every dimension is one.
The unweighted sum of morphism-space dimensions is bounded by the indicated opposite endomorphism dimension.
